Business plan text:

Kilnbright
Executive Summary
Kilnbright
A Smart Kiln Controller for Classroom Learning
Problem
In middle schools across America, art teachers have a problem with kilns. Kilns is very hot, up
to over two thousand degrees, and are danger if the teacher do not know how to use it correct.
Many teachers are not trained for firing ceramics and they are afraid of the kiln so some
schools dont even use there kiln at all and it sit in the corner. This is a big problem because
ceramics is a important part of art education and students loses the chance to make things with
there hands. Also the old kiln controllers is hard to understand with many buttons and numbers
and codes that the teacher must learn. When the teacher make mistake the pottery can break or
explode and this waste time and money and the students feels bad. Also the students do not
learn nothing about the science of heat during firing, which is a missed opportunity in STEM
education. We think this problem is very big and it need to be solved.
Solution
Kilnbright is the solution. It is a low cost digital kiln controller that is classroom safe.
The teacher just plug it into the kiln and choose a preset program like bisque or glaze and
push the button. Then Kilnbright do everything automatic and the teacher dont need to
understand the temperatures. It have a safety feature that shut off the kiln if it get too hot.
It also have a color screen who show the students what is happening inside the kiln and explain
the science of heat and glaze chemistry in a fun way. So Kilnbright is both a controller and a
education tool. We believe this is a innovative and disruptive solution that will change how
ceramics is taught. Our controller is easy, safe, smart, and fun, and it is the first to
combine all of these things together in one product for schools.
Market
The market for Kilnbright is very large. There is thousands of middle schools in the United
States and each one have a art teacher and many have a kiln. Education is a huge market worth
billions of dollars and technology in education is growing every year. If we get only one
percent of the market we will make a lot of money. Also there is private art studios, summer
camps, community centers, and hobby potters who might want our product too, so the market is
even bigger. We think the total market is over one billion dollars. Schools are always looking
for new STEM products because of the focus on STEM in education and the government give funding
for it. Teachers also buy things themselves with there own money for the classroom. The market
is growing and our timing is perfect because everybody is talking about STEM and hands on
learning right now.
Business Model
We will make money by selling the Kilnbright controller to schools and teachers. The price will
be about two hundred dollars which is low cost compared to other controllers. We will also sell
a subscription for lesson content and new firing programs, maybe around ten dollars a month,
but we have not decided yet the exact price. Later we might also sell accessories and other
products and maybe advertising or partnerships. We will sell online through our website and
also to school districts directly. We think many schools will buy it because it is cheap and
the teachers will tell other teachers about it so the sales will grow fast by word of mouth.
The hardware have a good margin and the subscription will make recurring revenue so the
business is scalable. We will figure out the details of the pricing after we talk to more
customers.
Competition

There is some competitors who sell kiln controllers but they are not like us. The existing
controllers is expensive, complicated, and made for professional potters not for classrooms.
They dont have education features and are not safe for kids. Some companies also make kilns
with built in controllers but this is more expensive and school must buy whole new kiln.
Because of this we think we have no real competition in the classroom market. Our competitive
advantage is that we are the only one who is focus on students and teachers and make it easy
and educational. Big companies could maybe copy us but we will be first to market and have the
brand. Also we have a website and we are working on getting patent protection for our idea,
which will protect us from competition.
Team
Dashiell Brownleigh is the CEO and is a junior studying business at our university. He is
passionate about education and entrepreneurship and he did a internship once. He lead the team
and do the strategy and sales.
Marisol Quentara is the CTO and is a senior studying electrical engineering at our university.
She build the prototype and know about electronics and sensors and programming. She is very
talented.
Tobias Wrenfield is head of product and a sophomore studying art education at our university.
He have experience with ceramics and understand the teachers needs because he took a pottery
class and work in the art department.
We are a strong team with business, technology, and art skills together and we work very hard.
We dont have yet a advisor but we are looking for mentors.
Milestones and Financials
So far we have defined our core business concept and we have build a working prototype of the
Kilnbright controller. The prototype can control a small kiln and run a preset program and show
the screen. We also raised some funding, about eight thousand dollars, from family and friends
and a small grant from our university. We have a website also. We have not formed a legal
entity yet but we will do it soon when we need it. We have not sold anything yet and so we have
no revenue at the moment. We have talked to some teachers who said they like the idea, but we
have not done formal customer research yet. For the next year we plan to improve the prototype,
make a bigger version, test in some schools, and start selling. We think we can have revenue of
one million dollars in three years and be profitable soon after, but we dont have a detailed
financial model yet. The cost to make each controller is maybe around eighty dollars but this
is a estimate and could change.
What We Are Asking For
We are asking for the prize money from this competition to help us grow Kilnbright. We would
use the money to build more prototypes, pay for safety certification, hire a manufacturer, and
do marketing. We are also asking for mentorship and connections to investors and schools and
any help with legal and business advice. We believe that Kilnbright can be a big success and
make a real impact in education and we are excited to join this competition. Thank you for
considering our application and we hope to be selected so we can take Kilnbright to the next
level and make ceramics safe and fun for every classroom in America.

Question: What can the team do to improve their written submission?

response.text:
The team can improve their written submission by:

1. **Clarifying the Problem Statement**: The problem is described in a disorganized and grammatically flawed manner. It should be restructured into a clear, concise, and impactful problem statement that highlights the gap in the market and the negative consequences of the current situation.

2. **Enhancing the Solution Description**: The solution is promising but lacks depth and specificity. The team should elaborate on the technical capabilities of Kilnbright, including how the safety features, educational content, and automation work in practice, and how they address the identified problems.

3. **Refining the Market Analysis**: The market section is vague and lacks data. The team should include specific numbers (e.g., number of schools, average kiln usage, potential adoption rates) and reference credible sources to strengthen the market size and growth potential claims.

4. **Improving the Business Model**: The business model is overly simplistic. The team should detail the pricing strategy, customer acquisition plan, revenue streams, and scalability factors with more precision and realism.

5. **Strengthening the Competitive Analysis**: The competitive section is weak and lacks depth. The team should conduct a more thorough analysis of competitors, including their strengths and weaknesses, and clearly articulate how Kilnbright differentiates itself.

6. **Polishing the Team Section**: The team section is brief and lacks depth. The team should highlight individual expertise, past experience, and how their combined skills create a competitive advantage.

7. **Enhancing the Financials and Milestones**: The financials and milestones are vague. The team should provide more detailed financial projections, cost structures, and a realistic timeline for product development, testing, and market entry.

8. **Improving Grammar, Tone, and Structure**: The submission contains numerous grammatical errors, awkward phrasing, and inconsistent tone. A professional, polished, and well-structured document will significantly enhance credibility and readability.

9. **Adding Visual Aids and Supporting Data**: Including diagrams, charts, or mockups of the product, along with data from customer feedback or market research, will strengthen the submission.

10. **Aligning with the Competition’s Criteria**: The team should ensure the submission aligns with the judging criteria of the competition, emphasizing innovation, market potential, scalability, and team capability.
